PullRequest.Title: automations: refactor: make provider session templates canonical

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Ownership and cleanup are explicit in the added method, and ChatModes cancellation occurs only in dispose. The trigger depends on slow or hung discovery, but extension-host/customization discovery is a real asynchronous boundary and recurrence makes the retention scaling deterministic once it stalls.
Findings.PerformanceResource: ChatModes instances, global event listeners, pending custom-agent discovery promises, and captured session/provider objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every fallback Automation draft or scheduled run whose saved mode is not immediately found, one independent ChatModes refresh is created. If discovery stalls, retained objects and listeners grow linearly with subsequent runs; simultaneous runs also issue concurrent discovery requests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: unbounded retained memory and listener/IPC growth while custom-agent discovery is stalled
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Fallback Automations supplied modeId through the management service's post-create setMode path. The provider performed a synchronous lookup with a temporary ChatModes instance and disposed it immediately, so no pending refresh survived the call.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Initial Automation configuration now launches `_resolveAutomationSessionMode` with `void`; that method owns a ChatModes instance but disposes it only after `waitForPendingUpdates()` settles, with no timeout or cancellation tied to deletion, replacement, send completion, or provider disposal.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1919 adds the unbounded `await modes.waitForPendingUpdates()` in a newly added fire-and-forget resolver; cleanup is reachable only after that await settles.
Findings.Title: Cancel fallback mode discovery with the draft lifecycle
Findings.Impact: If custom-agent discovery is hung or delayed by an unavailable/restarting extension host, each older-host/browser Automation run using an unresolved provider/custom mode leaves another ChatModes object, subscriptions, refresh token, and session closure alive. Recurring Automations then cause renderer memory and listener counts to grow for the lifetime of the stalled discovery.
Findings.Evidence: The added caller at line 1753 fire-and-forgets `_resolveAutomationSessionMode`. At lines 1917-1930 the method creates ChatModes, awaits its pending refresh, and only disposes in `finally`. ChatModes registers global customization, storage, configuration, and agent listeners; its `dispose()` is what cancels `_refreshCancellationSource`. Because no owner can dispose this local instance while the await is pending, cancellation is circular. `waitForPendingUpdates` awaits customizationHarnessService.getCustomAgents, an asynchronous extension/customization boundary.
Findings.Recommendation: Register the resolver/ChatModes instance with the draft or provider lifecycle and race pending discovery with that cancellation (and a bounded timeout). Dispose it immediately when the draft is replaced, deleted, committed, or the provider shuts down; also coalesce discovery where multiple runs resolve the same session scope.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open/edit an Automation and switch workspace, provider, or session type
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workspace selection validation completes, then the Automation draft synchronizer applies the latest target. The diff places previous-draft configuration capture before replacement draft creation, so pending Agent Host config resolution can delay the new controls by the one-second retarget bound.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider session configuration through Agent Host connection.resolveSessionConfig
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per concrete draft target; equal target updates are coalesced, target transitions are serialized, and returning to a target reuses cached captured configuration but still creates a new draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider draft resolution already occurred, but target replacement did not await the previous draft's resolution/capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Draft creation starts the resolution; the new retarget capture awaits the current draft's pending resolution before the replacement target can progress, bounded at 1,000 ms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve workspace target and trust information
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per distinct serialized workspace target update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same workspace validation preceded draft creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before a workspace draft can be created.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct provider/type/folder transitions while the dialog is open; equal updates collapse, but transitions arriving during a capture are serialized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronizer loop; no parallel target application. Provider capture for the prior draft is awaited before the next draft is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The latest captured configuration is cached by concrete target key for the dialog lifetime. Cold targets create drafts and resolve config; revisiting a target seeds from the cache but does not reuse the prior draft.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ordering, timeout, IPC call path, coalescing, and serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent Host response time varies; cold startup or degraded host connections can consume most of the explicit one-second bound.
Scenarios.Verdict: A concrete interaction-latency regression exists on retargeting; repeated report_finding submissions for this changed line failed at the reporting backend.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save an Automation after editing provider-owned controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Save waits for target synchronization and then one provider capture before constructing the result. Capture shares a five-second deadline and cancellation from Cancel/Escape/Close.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for Agent Host configuration resolution and capture the resolved template
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One final capture per Save attempt after synchronization; retries occur only after an explicit failed save attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Save waited only for draft synchronization and synchronously read legacy model/mode/permission selections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Save cannot complete until capture succeeds, fails, is cancelled, or reaches the five-second bound.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the resulting Automation update/create through the owning provider store
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mutation boundary persisted flattened fields rather than the complete provider template.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after dialog result handling in the existing create/update workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One capture and one mutation per explicit Save attempt; provider config size controls cloning/serialization work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Save is guarded by saveInProgress; duplicate submits are suppressed and cancellation is propagated to synchronization/capture.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm target capture uses the active resolved draft and per-target cached preferences. Failed capture does not overwrite the cache or close the dialog.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Capture latency depends on provider resolution; the five-second deadline bounds user-visible waiting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new save wait is intentional, cancellable, single-flight, and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run a canonical Automation through Agent Host or older-host/browser fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runner claims one active run per Automation, creates a draft with the canonical template, applies target-owned isolation, and sends the first request. Agent Host-owned execution already consumes AutomationDefinition.session directly; fallback now restores configuration at draft creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/resolve the provider session and send the Automation request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session dispatch per claimed run. Claims prevent duplicate concurrent runs for the same Automation; different Automations may run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback created the same session and request, then applied legacy model/mode/permission setters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing run-start critical path; passing the template changes payload/state but does not add another session dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new ChatModes refresh for every fallback draft/run whose saved mode is not immediately found; simultaneous Automations can issue these concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Post-create setMode performed an immediate lookup and disposed its temporary ChatModes object instead of awaiting discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget and therefore off the request-send critical path, but retained until discovery settles.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and recurrence of fallback Automations with unresolved provider/custom modes; retained work grows per run while discovery is stalled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single active run is enforced per Automation, but no cross-Automation limiter or coalescing exists for mode discovery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each resolver creates a separate ChatModes instance that loads workspace cached modes, but a cache miss starts a fresh discovery. There is no shared negative cache or lifecycle-owned pending resolver.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fire-and-forget caller, uncancelled await, ChatModes listeners, and dispose-only cancellation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal discovery may finish quickly; extension-host restart, failure, or a hung customization provider determines retention duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression submitted: unresolved discovery can retain one resolver, listeners, and session closure per recurring run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load, list, duplicate, and mutate Automations with provider templates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup parses the existing ledger/catalog and migrates legacy Copilot configurations in memory. Listing projects templates; configureAutomation validates/clones JSON and then performs one guarded storage/provider mutation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the Automation ledger through storage service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing ledger read at service initialization and one serialized ledger write per legacy-store mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ledger boundary stored schema v3 and flat configuration fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Startup/load and mutation persistence remain on their prior paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch Agent Host Automation create/update and wait for catalog acknowledgement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per provider-owned mutation; catalog updates can re-project all A entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dispatch occurred with smaller flattened configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mutation completion waits for acknowledgement as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate, clone, stringify, and stable-stringify opaque provider configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded clone/stringify per tool input plus several equality serializations per guarded mutation; tool input is limited to depth 32, 10,000 values, and 65,536 serialized characters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editable-state serialization handled only small flat fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation on explicit list/configure/mutation paths, not render/input loops.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation count A and provider config top-level/deep value count K. Projection now shallow-copies config per Automation catalog projection, while guarded equality stable-stringifies the changed Automation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutations are sequenced/guarded by existing store logic; no new burst across storage or Agent Host boundaries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog projections are recomputed on catalog changes; run windows and per-Automation run observables retain existing caches. Tool validation has no cross-invocation cache but enforces input bounds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added work, low for material user impact at realistic template sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical provider templates contain only a few keys, so the added allocation/serialization is unlikely to dominate despite worst-case bounds.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: added serialization is bounded and occurs on explicit mutation/list paths; full-config projection amplification is too small under realistic provider cardinality to meet the reporting threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use ordinary New Session controls and permission checks after shared-control refactoring
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New Session creates the same two menu toolbars through shared helpers. Phone combined-picker state reacts to provider changes. Tool approval decisions perform an additional in-memory managed-policy lookup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Toolbar creation per visible New Session/Automation surface and permission checks per tool decision.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are synchronous and scoped; mode-picker model entries are reference counted and disposed in a microtask after their final toolbar releases them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ScopedModePickerModelCache shares one model per session observable while views reconstruct and deletes entries after the final reference. No unbounded key retention was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; operations are in-memory and constant-time apart from existing menu rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: helper extraction preserves existing toolbar work, the scoped model cache has bounded lifecycle cleanup, and policy lookups are constant-time.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 52 changed files and relevant transitive paths. Submitted the fallback custom-mode discovery cleanup-lifecycle finding. Also established a concrete one-second retarget critical-path regression, but report_finding failed repeatedly for that changed-line anchor. No performance regression fix requiring blame was identified.
